basketball-game-shorts.sub: Match-Day Shorts Built to Finish the Season
prose: Game shorts are the pair a player wears when the scoreboard is on. They sit a touch longer than practice shorts, carry the same sublimated team colors as the jersey they pair with, and are cut so nothing shifts on a hard cut or a landing. The design is dyed into the fabric, so the side panels and waistband stripe stay exactly as sharp in March as they were in November.

The build reflects that. A double-stitched elastic waistband with an internal drawcord holds under contact, the side seams are gusseted so the leg opening never binds at full stride, and the hem is bar-tacked where shorts usually give out first. Florida programs play a long season in warm gyms, and this is the pair meant to survive all of it.

Game shorts are ordered to match a jersey, so we build both from the same color file. Your team's exact primary and accent colors are matched once and reused — no drift between the top and the bottom, and no surprise when next season's reorder arrives.

benefits.rest: — tops and shorts are printed from one color file, so the set never looks slightly off.
— the leg opening moves with a full stride instead of binding at the top of a jump.
— the hem and pocket corners are reinforced where game shorts normally fail first.
— stays put through contact without a visible tie on the front of the uniform.

basketball-game-shorts.cardSub: Full-color · Matched to your jersey · Any length
basketball-game-shorts.customizationIntro: Every element of your game shorts is fully customizable — side panels, waistband stripe, leg-hem trim, team name, player numbers, and sponsor marks. There are no pre-set templates and no color limits, and the artwork is built to sit correctly on a short rather than scaled down from a jersey design.
basketball-game-shorts.fabricIntro: Game shorts are made from the same sublimation polyester as the jersey they pair with, so the set matches under gym lighting. The weight is chosen for a warm Florida gym in the fourth quarter — light enough to breathe, heavy enough to hang properly rather than cling.
basketball-game-shorts.sizingIntro: Shorts are sized on waist and hip measurements, not chest. Measure around the natural waist where the band will sit, then check the inseam column for the length your program prefers. When a player is between sizes, size up — the drawcord takes in the waist, but nobody can add length.
basketball-game-shorts.bestForIntro: Game shorts are the right choice for teams buying a matched uniform set — a jersey and short that read as one design. If you only need bottoms for the practice floor, a lighter and cheaper pair will serve you better.
basketball-game-shorts.notFitIntro: Game shorts are built for match day. If most of your wear is drills and scrimmages, you are paying for a finish you will not see — these alternatives cost less and hold up just as well in practice.

sublimation.desc: Game shorts default to our standard sublimation polyester because a closed, smooth face is what makes a short hang correctly. On match day the short is seen standing still as often as moving — free throws, timeouts, the huddle — and a closed knit holds its line where an open one collapses against the leg.
pros: Hangs rather than clings — the short keeps its shape on a stationary player
Sharpest side-panel reproduction — fine stripes and piping stay crisp
Matches the jersey exactly — same fabric, same dye run, same fade over a season

wicking.desc: The wicking option adds 8% spandex, which shows up in a deep defensive stance more than anywhere else. Programs that play a lot of switching defence often prefer it for the extra give through the seat and thigh.
pros: 4-way stretch with spandex — more give in a low stance
Moves sweat by fibre channel — works in cool, air-conditioned gyms
Slightly lighter at 145 GSM against 155

mesh.desc: Mesh is available on game shorts, and worth it if your home venue runs hot. The trade is a visibly open weave, which reads less formal under arena lighting than the closed knit most programs choose for match day.
pros: Coolest option by a distance — the choice if your gym has no air conditioning
Dries between games on a tournament Saturday
Reads casual — the reason it is not the default here

audience.title: Teams Buying a Matched Uniform Set
audience.desc: This is the short designed to go with a jersey rather than alongside one. Both are printed from the same colour file in the same run, which is the only reliable way to stop a set looking almost-matched.
points: Side panels line up between top and short
One stored colour for both pieces
Reorders in later seasons still match

audience.title: Varsity and JV Programs
audience.desc: A school running two squads needs kit that reads as one program across both. Game shorts hold a formal line under arena lighting in a way a practice or mesh short does not.
points: Mixed adult and youth sizes on one order
School colours matched from a style guide
Numbers on the leg optional and sized to your league

audience.title: Travel and AAU Rosters
audience.desc: Tournament play is hard on shorts — three games a day, hotel laundry, a bag that lives in a car. The bar-tacked hem and gusseted seams are what survive that, though a second pair per player is worth budgeting.
points: Reinforced at the two points that fail first
Sublimated colour survives hotel washing
Second pair costs less than a mid-season replacement

customization.title: Side Panel Design
customization.desc: The side panel is what an audience actually sees of a short. On a game short it usually continues a line from the jersey rather than standing alone, which is why we build both from one artwork file.

customization.title: Waistband Treatment
customization.desc: Visible whether the jersey is tucked or not. Most game shorts use a plain matched band and put the design work into the side panel, but a team-name repeat is available.

customization.title: Leg Numbers
customization.desc: Some leagues require a number on the short as well as the jersey. Check your rulebook before ordering — adding them after the fact means a reprint, not a patch.

customization.title: Inseam Length
customization.desc: Specify it once and the whole run matches. Nine inches is what most Florida adult programs order; youth squads usually take seven.

customization.title: Pocket Options
customization.desc: Game shorts ship without pockets by default, because most leagues prohibit them on court. They can be added for warm-up or coaching versions of the same design.

customization.title: Colour Matching
customization.desc: Send the jersey, a Pantone value or a previous order. The match is made once and stored, which is what keeps a set together across seasons.

construction.title: Gusseted Side Seams
construction.body: A triangular panel set into the side seam widens the leg opening as the player strides. On a closed knit this is what prevents the hem pulling across the thigh at the top of a jump.

construction.title: Bar-Tacked Hem Corners
construction.body: The hem split takes more stress than any other point on a game short. Both corners carry a dense bar-tack, which is the difference between a short that lasts a season and one that starts fraying in January.

construction.title: Double-Stitched Waistband
construction.body: The waistband is stitched twice along its full length rather than once. It is the seam that carries the whole garment's weight and the one that gives out first on cheaper shorts.

construction.title: Internal Drawcord Channel
construction.body: The cord runs inside the band and never exits at the front. Nothing is visible on the outside of a match-day short, and there is no tie to work loose during contact.

care.text: Machine wash cold, inside out — protects the printed side panels from abrasion.
Wash with like colours — a matched set should be laundered together to age together.
Air dry — a closed knit holds its line better without heat.
No fabric softener — it leaves a film that dulls printed colour over a season.
No ironing on the panel — direct heat on sublimated artwork is the one thing that can damage it.
Do not bleach — bleach attacks the dye, not dirt, on a sublimated garment.

basketball-game-shorts.floridaNote: Match day in a Florida gym: most high school venues in the state are air-conditioned and a closed knit is the right call — it holds a formal line and the heat is handled by the building. If your home court is outdoor, or a hall without working air conditioning, order this same design in mesh instead: identical artwork, identical colours, a fabric that lets the heat out.

measure.title: How to Measure — Game Shorts
steps: Waist: Measure around the natural waist where the band sits, just above the hip bone. Do not measure at the belly button.
Hip: Measure the fullest part of the seat with feet together — this decides comfort in a defensive stance more than the waist does.
Inseam: From the crotch seam down the inner leg to the hem you want. Nine inches is standard for adult Florida programs.
Match to the jersey: Order both together so the run is printed from one file. A player may take different sizes top and bottom.

basketball-practice-shorts.sub: Everyday Shorts for Four Sessions a Week
prose: Practice shorts are the pair that goes in the wash four times a week. They are cut a little shorter and looser than game shorts, printed in a simpler one- or two-color scheme, and priced so a program can buy two pairs per player without touching the uniform budget. Durability matters more than detail here, and the build reflects that.

Because they are washed constantly, the seams are the part we over-build: double-needle stitching on the waistband and hem, and a fabric chosen for how it looks after fifty washes rather than on day one. Sublimated color does not fade in a hot wash the way a screen-printed logo does, which is exactly why practice gear is worth sublimating.

Most Florida programs order these in the team's base color with a number on the leg, so a coach can call a player across the gym without squinting. Numbers can repeat across squads — practice shorts do not have to follow league roster rules the way game shorts do.

benefits.rest: — sublimated color survives hot cycles that strip screen-printed logos in a season.

benefits.strong: Priced for two pairs per player
benefits.rest: — so nobody is practicing in yesterday's shorts on a back-to-back day.
— the two seams that fail first on practice gear are the two we reinforce.
— easy to identify players across a full gym without game-day roster rules.

basketball-practice-shorts.cardSub: Wash-durable · Simple color scheme · Team pricing
basketball-practice-shorts.customizationIntro: Practice shorts keep customization deliberately simple — a base color, one accent, and an optional leg number. You can still specify exact team colors, but the simpler layout is what keeps these affordable enough to order two pairs per player.
basketball-practice-shorts.fabricIntro: These are built from a hard-wearing polyester chosen for wash cycles, not for photographs. It is the same fiber family as the game shorts, in a weight that dries fast between back-to-back sessions in a humid Florida gym.
basketball-practice-shorts.sizingIntro: Practice shorts run slightly looser than game shorts at the same size, which most players prefer for drills. Measure the natural waist and match the closest size. If your program wants one order to cover growth across a season, size up for younger players.
basketball-practice-shorts.bestForIntro: Practice shorts make sense for any program where players train more often than they play — which is nearly all of them. If you need a pair that matches your game jersey exactly, order game shorts instead.
basketball-practice-shorts.notFitIntro: These are not built to match a game jersey panel-for-panel. If the shorts will be worn on match day alongside a sublimated top, choose from these instead.

sublimation.desc: Practice shorts are judged on wash cycles, not on photographs, and the standard polyester is the most wash-durable fabric we offer. Fifty hot cycles is the test, and a closed knit at 155 GSM comes through it looking like kit rather than like something recovered from a lost-property bin.
pros: Most durable of our fabrics — built for four washes a week
Resists pilling where a lighter knit fuzzes
Cheapest to reorder mid-season when a pair goes missing

mesh.desc: Worth choosing if your practice court is outdoors or your gym has no air conditioning. Mesh trades some durability for a lot of airflow, which on a daily-use garment is a real trade rather than a free upgrade.
pros: Much cooler for outdoor sessions
Dries overnight between back-to-back days
Snags more easily — the honest cost of an open weave

audience.title: Programs Buying Two Pairs Per Player
audience.desc: The whole point of a practice short is that there is a clean one tomorrow. These are priced so a squad of fifteen can have thirty pairs without touching the uniform budget.
points: No minimum order
Same price whether you order 15 or 60
Reorder a single pair mid-season without a setup charge

audience.title: Daily Training and Drill Work
audience.desc: Four sessions a week for four months is roughly seventy wears and seventy washes. Everything here is built around that number rather than around how the short looks on day one.
points: Double-needle waistband and hem
Sublimated colour cannot crack in a hot wash
Simple layout keeps the price where it needs to be

audience.title: Camps and Clinics
audience.desc: A summer camp needs kit that identifies groups and survives a week of hard use. Two contrasting colours split a session instantly, and numbers may repeat because nobody is checking a roster.
points: Two-colour orders split squads without pinnies
Numbers can repeat across colours
Cheap enough to send home with participants

audience.title: Match-Day Wear
audience.desc: These will not match a game jersey panel for panel — the layout is deliberately simpler and the colour is matched to your base rather than to a specific set. They are practice kit, and they look like it.
points: Order game shorts for match day
Or run practice shorts in the same base colour
Both can be printed from one stored colour

customization.title: Two-Colour Squad Split
customization.desc: The single most useful thing you can specify on a practice order. Half the run in one colour, half in another, and five-on-five takes thirty seconds instead of a hunt for pinnies.

customization.title: Leg Numbers
customization.desc: Practice numbers are printed larger than game numbers on purpose. A coach calls a player from the far baseline, not from the scorer's table.

customization.title: Base Colour and Accent
customization.desc: Practice kit keeps to two colours because that is what keeps it cheap. Your team base plus one accent is the standard layout here.

customization.title: Waistband
customization.desc: A plain matched band on practice shorts, almost always. The budget is better spent on a second pair than on a printed waistband nobody sees at training.

construction.title: Double-Needle Waistband
construction.body: Two parallel rows of stitching along the full band. On a garment washed four times a week this is the seam that decides its life, and it is the first place a cheap practice short comes apart.

construction.title: Double-Needle Hem
construction.body: The hem takes the same treatment for the same reason. A single-stitched hem on a daily-use short unravels from one broken thread; a double row does not.

construction.title: Reinforced Crotch Seam
construction.body: The four-way seam junction is the highest-stress point on any short. An extra pass of stitching there is what stops a split during a lunge in the third week of preseason.

construction.title: Colourfast Sublimated Dye
construction.body: The colour is inside the fibre rather than on it. Seventy hot washes will not fade it, which is the whole argument for sublimating practice kit rather than screen-printing it.

care.text: Hot wash is fine — sublimated colour is unaffected, and practice kit needs it.
Tumble dry low — these are the one garment here built to take a dryer.
Wash colours separately if you ordered a two-colour squad split.
No fabric softener — it builds up on daily-washed kit faster than on anything else.
Do not bleach — it attacks the dye rather than the stain.
No high-heat drying — low is fine; high relaxes the waistband over a season.

basketball-practice-shorts.floridaNote: Practice in Florida means humidity, not just heat. A short that does not dry overnight goes on damp the next day, and that is how a program ends up with kit that smells by October. These dry fast enough to hang on a rail at 6pm and be ready at 6am — and if your training court is outdoors, order the mesh version instead and accept the trade in durability.

measure.title: How to Measure — Practice Shorts
steps: Waist: Around the natural waist. Practice shorts run looser than game shorts at the same size, which most players prefer.
Hip: The fullest part of the seat. If a player is between sizes here rather than at the waist, size up.
Growing players: For a youth programme buying one order to last a season, size up. The drawcord covers the difference in November.
Two pairs: Order the same size twice rather than one of each — a player wearing two different fits notices.

prose: Mesh shorts use an open-weave knit that moves air through the fabric instead of trapping it. Hold a pair to the light and you can see the structure — thousands of small gaps that let heat off the skin. In a Miami or Orlando gym in August, that difference is the one players actually notice.

The trade-off with mesh is usually opacity and shape, and both are handled in the build. A bonded inner panel keeps the short opaque where it needs to be, and the knit is stabilized so the leg keeps its line instead of collapsing after a few washes. The result breathes like mesh and hangs like a solid short.

Mesh takes sublimation differently from a flat knit — the dye has to bridge the weave. We print these with a heavier ink lay-down so the color reads solid at arm's length, which is why a mesh short from a proper sublimation run looks nothing like a stock mesh short with a heat-pressed number.

benefits.rest: — heat leaves through the fabric rather than sitting against the skin in a warm gym.
— keeps the short fully opaque without giving up the breathability that makes mesh worth it.
— color reads solid across the weave instead of looking washed out at a distance.
— an open knit sheds moisture far quicker than a flat, dense short.

mesh-basketball-shorts.customizationIntro: Mesh takes color differently from a flat knit, so the artwork is prepared for the weave rather than simply reused from a jersey file. Side panels, waistband stripes, and leg numbers all print full-color, and we adjust the ink lay-down so the design reads solid on an open fabric.
mesh-basketball-shorts.fabricIntro: These are built from athletic mesh — an open knit whose whole purpose is airflow. It is the lightest fabric we offer for shorts and the fastest drying, which is why it is the default recommendation for outdoor courts and un-air-conditioned gyms in Florida.
mesh-basketball-shorts.sizingIntro: Mesh has more give than a flat knit, so most players take their usual size rather than sizing up. Measure the natural waist. If the shorts will be worn over compression tights in winter training, allow one size of room.
mesh-basketball-shorts.bestForIntro: Mesh shorts are the right call for teams playing in heat — outdoor courts, summer league, preseason conditioning, and any gym without real air conditioning. For a formal match-day set, a flat-knit game short holds a crisper line.
mesh-basketball-shorts.notFitIntro: Mesh is built for airflow, not for a structured match-day look. If your program wants a sharper, more formal short, these are the better fit.

mesh.desc: Athletic mesh is the reason these shorts exist. The knit is built with thousands of deliberate openings rather than a closed face, so warm air leaves through the fabric instead of collecting against the thigh. On a short this matters more than on a top: the leg is a large muscle group generating heat through every possession, and it is the area most players report as the first place they overheat.
pros: Air moves through the leg panel — heat leaves rather than pooling against the thigh
Bonded inner panel — the short stays fully opaque without closing the weave
Dries between games — an open knit sheds moisture far faster than a closed one
Heavier ink lay-down — colour reads solid across the weave instead of dotted

wicking.desc: The moisture-wicking option closes the weave and moves sweat chemically instead of letting air through it. On shorts this is the better answer for an air-conditioned gym in January, where airflow is not the problem and a closed face holds a sharper line for match play.
pros: Closed face, sharper line — holds its shape better than mesh under gym lighting
Moves sweat by fibre channel — works when the air around the player is already cool
Slight stretch content — 8% spandex gives more give through a deep defensive stance

sublimation.desc: Our standard sublimation polyester is the middle option: a closed, smooth face that reproduces artwork most precisely. If your shorts carry a detailed side panel or a fine sponsor mark, this is the fabric that will hold it, at the cost of the airflow mesh gives you.
pros: Sharpest artwork reproduction — a smooth face holds fine type and thin outlines
Most structured drape — the short hangs rather than clings on a still player
Hardest wearing of the three — the right pick if the same pair is worn daily

audience.title: Outdoor and Un-Air-Conditioned Courts
audience.desc: This is the situation mesh shorts were built for. Florida park courts, church gyms and school auxiliary halls regularly run ten to fifteen degrees warmer than a main arena, and the leg is where players feel it first.
points: Air moves through the panel rather than trapping heat
Dries fast enough for a second game the same day
Bonded panel keeps the short opaque in bright sun

audience.title: Summer League and July Camps
audience.desc: A summer roster plays more basketball in six weeks than a school season fits in three months, usually in the hottest venues on the calendar. Mesh is the single change that makes that schedule bearable.
points: Three games a day on one pair
Washes and dries overnight between camp days
No minimum order, so a six-week roster is economic

audience.title: Programs With High-Sweat Players
audience.desc: Every roster has two or three players who run visibly hotter than the rest. Ordering the whole squad in mesh costs the same as ordering them in anything else, and solves it without singling anyone out.
points: Same price as a closed-knit short
No separate order or different-looking kit
Pairs with a mesh tank for a full open-weave set

audience.title: Formal Match-Day Sets
audience.desc: Mesh reads casual next to a closed knit — the weave is visible at a few feet, and a program that wants the sharpest possible look on a main court usually notices. It performs; it just does not photograph as crisply.
points: Consider a wicking or sublimation short for main-court games
Or run mesh for summer and a closed knit for the season
Both can be printed from the same colour file

customization.title: Side Panel Design
customization.desc: The side panel is the most visible surface on a pair of shorts from the stands, and on mesh it is the panel that carries the team's identity. Solid blocks, tapered stripes and full-length gradients all print here.

customization.title: Waistband Treatment
customization.desc: The waistband is the one part of a short that is always visible, including when a jersey is untucked. Team name, a repeat pattern or a plain contrast band are all available; the drawcord is internal either way.

customization.title: Leg Numbers
customization.desc: A number on the leg lets a coach identify a player across a full gym when the jersey is turned away. Practice programs use these constantly; game shorts usually keep them smaller or leave them off.

customization.title: Inseam Length
customization.desc: Inseam is a fit decision as much as a style one, and it is the thing most often left to chance in a team order. Specify it once and every pair in the run matches.

customization.title: Colour Matching
customization.desc: Shorts almost always have to match a top that already exists. Send the jersey, a Pantone value or a previous order and the colour is matched to it and stored for reorders.

measure.title: How to Measure — Shorts
steps: Waist: Measure around the natural waist, where the band will actually sit — usually just above the hip bone, not at the belly button.
Hip: Measure around the fullest part of the seat with feet together. On a short this matters more than waist for comfort in a defensive stance.
Inseam: Measure from the crotch seam down the inner leg to where you want the hem to finish. Most Florida programs specify 9 inches for adults.
Between sizes: Size up. The internal drawcord takes in a waist that is slightly loose; nothing can add length to a short that is too small.

construction.title: Gusseted Side Seams
construction.body: A triangular panel is set into the side seam so the leg opening widens as the player strides. Without it, a mesh short binds at the top of a jump — the open knit has less give in the direction the seam runs, which is exactly where a closed-knit short would stretch.

construction.title: Bonded Inner Panel
construction.body: The front and seat panels carry a second bonded layer. This is what lets the rest of the short stay fully open: opacity is solved locally rather than by closing the whole weave, so the leg keeps its airflow.

construction.title: Bar-Tacked Hem Corners
construction.body: The two hem corners take the most stress on any pair of shorts, and on an open knit they are also the weakest point. Each is bar-tacked — a dense cluster of stitches — which is why these do not start unravelling at the split.

construction.title: Internal Drawcord
construction.body: The drawcord runs inside a channel in the waistband rather than exiting at the front. Nothing is visible on the outside of the short, and there is no tie to come loose or catch during contact.

care.text: Machine wash cold — an open knit releases sweat and salt easily, so a cold cycle is enough.
Wash inside out — protects the bonded inner panel from abrasion against zips and studs.
Air dry — mesh dries in minutes in Florida air; a dryer is genuinely unnecessary.
No fabric softener — it coats the weave and closes the openings that make these worth buying.
No high-heat drying — heat relaxes the knit and the leg opening loses its shape.
Do not wash with hook-and-loop — velcro on other kit will snag an open weave every time.

mesh-basketball-shorts.floridaNote: Why mesh, in this state specifically: a closed-knit short holds a layer of warm, humid air against the thigh, and Florida gives you humid air to start with. An open weave lets that layer move. On an outdoor court in July the fabric is doing more work than any other choice on the order form — and because it dries in minutes in this climate, one pair genuinely covers a three-game Saturday.

lightweight-basketball-shorts.sub: The Lightest Short We Make, Cut for Speed
prose: Lightweight shorts strip out weight everywhere it is not doing work. The fabric is a thinner gauge of the same performance polyester, the waistband is narrower, and the hem is single-folded rather than banded. On the floor it reads as less material moving with the player on every change of direction.

This is a guard's short. Programs that run a fast tempo, and players who spend the game in transition, tend to ask for exactly this: minimum fabric, maximum range, nothing flapping at the knee. It is also the coolest option after mesh, simply because there is less of it.

Lighter fabric is less forgiving of poor construction, so the seams do more of the work. Flatlock seams sit flush against the skin instead of standing proud, which matters more here than on a heavier short where the fabric hides the seam.

benefits.rest: — noticeably less weight on the leg through a full game of transition play.
— sit flush against the skin, which a light fabric cannot disguise the way a heavy one can.
— less bulk at the hip when the shorts are worn under a warm-up or over tights.
— useful for travel rosters carrying two changes to a multi-game weekend.

lightweight-basketball-shorts.customizationIntro: A lighter fabric shows artwork cleanly, so these take detailed designs well — gradients, fades, and multi-color side panels all print sharply. Team name, numbers, and sponsor marks are placed to sit correctly on a shorter, narrower panel.
lightweight-basketball-shorts.fabricIntro: Built from a thinner gauge of our moisture-wicking performance polyester. It carries the same sweat-pull behavior as our standard weight with less material, which is what makes it the lightest non-mesh short we produce.
lightweight-basketball-shorts.sizingIntro: Lightweight shorts are cut close, so a player who prefers a roomier short should size up. Measure the natural waist and check the inseam column — this style is most often ordered one inch shorter than a standard game short.
lightweight-basketball-shorts.bestForIntro: These suit fast-tempo programs and players who dislike extra fabric. If your team plays a physical, contact-heavy style, a standard-weight game short will take the abuse better.
lightweight-basketball-shorts.notFitIntro: A lighter fabric is not the toughest option in a contact-heavy program. If your shorts take a beating every session, these will last longer.

wicking.desc: The lightweight short is built on the wicking knit rather than the standard one, and the 8% spandex is the reason. Take fabric away from a short and it needs to stretch more, not less — there is less material to accommodate a stride, so the give has to come from the fibre.
pros: 4-way stretch — carries the range a thin fabric would otherwise lose
145 GSM against 155 — the weight saving you can actually feel
Moves sweat by fibre channel rather than relying on airflow

mesh.desc: Lighter still, but a different kind of light: mesh removes material by opening the weave where this short removes it by thinning the yarn. Mesh is cooler; this is closer-fitting and holds a cleaner line.
pros: Coolest of the three for outdoor play
Less structured — reads casual next to a thin closed knit
Snags more easily on benches and racks

sublimation.desc: The standard weight is here for programmes that want the same design in a tougher short. Ten extra GSM does not sound like much and is very noticeable over a season of daily contact work.
pros: Most durable — the right call if one pair does everything
Sharpest artwork on a smooth closed face
Heavier on the leg — the trade you are making

audience.title: Guards and Fast-Tempo Programs
audience.desc: A team that spends the game in transition notices fabric weight in the fourth quarter. Less material on the leg is not a marketing claim at that tempo — it is the difference players report first.
points: Least weight of any closed-knit short we make
Flatlock seams sit flush at speed
Cut narrower through the thigh

audience.title: Layering Over Compression Tights
audience.desc: Programs that run compression underneath need a short that does not add bulk at the hip. The narrow waistband is built for exactly that stack.
points: Narrow band reduces bulk at the waist
Size up one for a comfortable stack
Works with full-length or three-quarter tights

audience.title: Contact-Heavy Programs
audience.desc: A thinner yarn is a thinner yarn. If your squad plays a physical style and one pair does every session, the standard-weight short will outlast this by a clear margin.
points: Order game or training shorts for heavy contact
Or buy two pairs of these for the same money
Same artwork either way

customization.title: Side Panel Design
customization.desc: A narrow panel on a shorter cut, so designs that work on a game short can crowd here. We adjust the artwork to the panel rather than scaling it down.

customization.title: Inseam Length
customization.desc: This style is most often ordered an inch shorter than a standard game short. Seven inches is the common request for guards.

customization.title: Waistband Width
customization.desc: Narrow by default, because bulk at the hip is what this short is built to avoid. A standard band is available if the short is worn on its own.

customization.title: Colour Matching
customization.desc: Match to an existing top or a Pantone value. Stored once and reused so a later reorder is the same shade.

construction.title: Flatlock Seams Throughout
construction.body: Every seam is laid flat rather than stood proud. On a thin fabric there is nothing to hide a raised seam — what a heavier short absorbs, this one would press into the skin over a full game.

construction.title: Narrow Bonded Waistband
construction.body: The band is narrower and bonded rather than folded, which removes a layer at the hip. That is where a short worn over tights bunches, and where the bulk would otherwise show under a jersey.

construction.title: Single-Fold Hem
construction.body: A single fold rather than a banded hem, taking weight off the leg opening. It is why the hem moves with the stride instead of swinging behind it.

care.text: Cold wash, inside out — a thin knit is more exposed to abrasion in a full machine.
Air dry — heat is harder on a light yarn than on a heavy one.
Wash with like fabrics — zips and studs find a thin short first.

training-basketball-shorts.sub: Off-Court Shorts for Conditioning and Weights
prose: Training shorts are for the work that happens away from the court — the weight room, sprint work, conditioning blocks, and preseason. They are cut with a little more room through the thigh than a game short, so a squat or a lunge does not pull the hem, and they are built to be worn several times a week for months.

The differences are practical. The waistband is wider and higher so it stays put under a barbell, the inseam runs slightly longer for coverage during floor work, and the fabric is a denser knit that resists snagging on gym equipment far better than an open mesh would.

Programs usually order these in the team base color with a small mark rather than full uniform artwork, because they are worn where nobody is checking numbers. The point is that everyone in the program looks like they belong to it, in every setting, not only on game night.

prose: A short-sleeve basketball shirt is the layer worn over the jersey before tip-off and on the bench between rotations. Because it is worn off the floor, the cut is roomier through the chest and shoulder than a game jersey so it pulls on over one. The hem sits straight rather than tapered, and the sleeve ends above the elbow so it does not interfere with a warm-up routine.

Sublimation matters more here than almost anywhere else on a uniform order. A shooting shirt is photographed constantly — team pictures, socials, senior night — and a heat-pressed logo starts cracking by January while a dyed one looks the same in the last game as the first.

moisture-wicking-basketball-shirt.sub: Engineered to Pull Sweat Off the Skin, Not Hold It
prose: Moisture-wicking is not a coating, and it is not a marketing word for polyester. It is a fiber cross-section engineered with channels that draw liquid along their length by capillary action and spread it across the outer surface, where a much larger area lets it evaporate. Cotton does the opposite: it absorbs and holds.

The practical difference shows up in the third quarter. A cotton or basic-polyester shirt has taken on weight and is clinging; a wicking shirt has moved that sweat to its outer face and is drying. In a Florida gym in February, that is still the difference between comfortable and soaked.

The finish is durable rather than applied, so it survives the wash. A shirt that wicks because of how its fiber is built will still wick after a hundred cycles, which is not true of shirts treated with a topical finish that rinses away.

lightweight-basketball-shirt.sub: The Thinnest Shirt We Make, for the Hottest Gyms
prose: This is the same performance knit as our standard shirt, spun to a thinner gauge. Less fabric means less to trap heat, less to hold sweat, and less weight on the shoulder over a two-hour session. Held up to the light it is noticeably more translucent — that is the trade being made, and it is a deliberate one.

Programs order these for the hottest part of a Florida calendar: August conditioning, summer league, and any venue where the air conditioning is decorative. They are also the shirt most often chosen as an under-jersey base layer, because thinner fabric adds nothing at the shoulder seam.

Thin fabric is unforgiving of cheap construction, so the seams do the work. Flatlock shoulder seams sit flush rather than standing proud, which on a light shirt is the difference between comfortable and abrasive over a long session.

sleeveless-basketball-tank-top.sub: Standard Basketball Cut, Full Shoulder Freedom
prose: A sleeveless tank is the classic basketball silhouette — armholes cut high and open so the shoulder rotates through a full shooting motion with nothing touching it. It is the cut most players default to, and the one most leagues picture when they write a uniform rule.

The armhole is where a tank is won or lost. Cut too shallow and it binds at the top of a shot; cut too deep and it gapes and shows the side. Ours is set at a standard competitive depth with a bound edge that keeps its shape rather than curling after a few washes.

Because there are no sleeves, the whole front and back are one uninterrupted print area. Full-color designs run edge to edge with no seam breaking them up, which is why sublimated tanks photograph better than almost anything else in a uniform order.

mesh-basketball-tank-top.sub: The Coolest Thing You Can Put a Player In
prose: A mesh tank combines the two coolest choices available: an open-weave fabric and a cut that leaves the shoulders bare. If a player is overheating in a Florida gym and you can only change one thing, this is the change.

The knit is an engineered open weave — thousands of deliberate gaps that let body heat leave rather than collect. A bonded front panel keeps the tank opaque across the chest and number area while the side and back panels stay fully open, so it breathes where it matters and covers where it must.

Printing on mesh is its own problem, because the dye has to bridge the weave rather than sit on a flat face. We increase the ink lay-down for mesh runs so numbers stay legible from the far bleachers instead of looking dotted at a distance.

performance-basketball-tank-top.sub: Competition Cut, Built Around Sweat Management
prose: A performance tank is the competition version of the sleeveless cut: the same shoulder freedom, built from moisture-wicking fiber and finished to a higher standard. Where a standard tank is judged on how it looks, this one is judged on how it behaves in the fourth quarter.

Three things separate it. The fabric is engineered to move sweat off the skin rather than hold it, the side panels are cut from a lighter contrast knit so the hottest part of the torso vents, and every seam is flatlocked so nothing abrades over a long game.

This is what most competitive Florida programs order for game day when the budget allows it. The difference over a season is not dramatic on any single night — it is that players stop mentioning the uniform at all, which is exactly what a uniform should do.

prose: A reversible uniform is two complete kits bonded into one garment. Turn the jersey inside out and the light home set becomes the dark away set, numbers and all; the shorts do the same. For a program that would otherwise buy and carry two sets, it halves both the cost and the bag.

It is a genuinely harder garment to make well. Both faces have to be finished, both sets of numbers have to align, and the bonded layers must not curl at the armhole or hem after a season of being turned. Ours are built with a bonded double layer and bound edges specifically so they do not.

The trade-off is honest: a reversible is slightly heavier and warmer than a single-layer jersey, because it is two fabrics. In an air-conditioned gym that is nothing. In an outdoor August tournament in Florida, a single-layer set will be more comfortable.

sublimated-basketball-jerseys.sub: Full-Dye Jerseys Where the Design Is the Fabric
prose: Dye sublimation turns solid dye directly into gas under heat and pressure, and that gas bonds with the polyester at a molecular level. The design does not sit on the jersey; it becomes part of the fiber. Run a fingernail across a sublimated number and you feel fabric, not a raised patch.

That single fact decides everything else. There is nothing on the surface to crack, peel, or wash off, no vinyl edge to lift after twenty games, and no weight added where the graphic sits. It also means color can run right to the seam — edge-to-edge, no white borders, no template limits.

The catch is that it only works on polyester, and it only works on light grounds — you cannot sublimate a light design onto a black jersey. Everything else about it is why this is the standard for competitive basketball kit, and why every other jersey we make is built from the same process.

sublimated-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Sublimation only bonds to polyester, so every jersey here is 100% sublimation polyester. That is a requirement of the process rather than a cost decision, and it is why these jerseys behave consistently in a hot Florida gym.
sublimated-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Measure the chest at the fullest point with arms relaxed. Sublimated jerseys do not shrink — polyester holds its dimensions through hot washes — so order the size you want to wear rather than allowing for shrinkage.
sublimated-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Sublimated jerseys suit almost every competitive situation: game day, school programs, travel and AAU. Where they do not fit is a team that needs jerseys decorated locally later, or one that wants a very dark ground with light artwork.
sublimated-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Sublimation needs a polyester ground and works from light to dark. If you plan to decorate locally later, or want a plain solid jersey, these are the better route.

prose: A reversible jersey is two finished jerseys bonded back to back. Turn it inside out and the light home top becomes the dark away top — same player, same number, opposite color. For any program that needs both and can only fund one, that is the whole argument.

It is the hardest jersey to build properly. Both faces must be fully finished, the numbers on each side have to sit in register so neither reads as the reverse of the other, and the bonded layers have to stay flat at the armhole and hem after a season of being turned. Bound edges are what keep them from curling.

Be clear about the trade: two fabrics are warmer than one. In an air-conditioned gym it is unnoticeable; in an outdoor August tournament it is not. Reversibles are a travel and tournament answer more than a hot-weather one.

benefits.rest: — home and away without funding, packing, or washing two separate sets.
— both faces are properly finished, so neither looks like the back of the other.
— the armhole and hem do not curl after a season of being turned inside out.
— five-on-five in scrimmage without a single pinnie leaving the bag.

reversible-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: You are designing two jerseys, not one — usually a light home face and a dark away face, though two completely different designs are equally possible. Names, numbers and logos are placed on both faces and aligned so neither side gives away the other.
reversible-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Reversibles use a bonded double-layer construction — two sublimated faces joined so neither shows through the other. This is heavier and warmer than a single-layer jersey by design; that weight is the price of carrying two kits in one.
reversible-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: A reversible sits a little fuller than a single-layer jersey. Most players take their usual chest size; a player who wants a very close fit should size down. Check the armhole column if your league specifies a maximum depth.
reversible-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Reversibles are built for travel rosters, tournament weekends, and programs working from one budget. In a hot, un-air-conditioned Florida gym, a single-layer jersey will be more comfortable.
reversible-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Two bonded layers run warmer than one. If your gyms are hot or your season is a summer one, these are the cooler choice.

prose: Mesh is an engineered open knit — thousands of deliberate gaps that let body heat leave through the fabric instead of collecting against the skin. It is the single most effective fabric change you can make for a team playing in Florida heat, and the difference is obvious inside ten minutes of play.

Two things make a mesh jersey work rather than just be thin. A bonded front panel keeps the chest and number area opaque while the sides and back stay fully open, and the knit is stabilized so the armhole and hem hold their line rather than collapsing after a few washes.

Printing on an open weave is its own craft. The dye has to bridge the gaps instead of landing on a flat face, so we increase the ink lay-down for mesh runs — which is why a properly sublimated mesh jersey reads solid from the bleachers where a stock mesh top looks dotted.

benefits.rest: — heat leaves through the fabric rather than sitting against the skin in a warm gym.
— chest and number area stay opaque while the sides and back remain fully open.
— numbers read solidly from the bleachers instead of looking dotted across the weave.
— which matters on a three-game tournament Saturday with one kit per player.

mesh-basketball-jerseys.cardSub: Open weave · Maximum airflow · Bonded front
mesh-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Artwork for mesh is prepared for the weave rather than reused from a flat-knit file. Names and numbers sit on the bonded panels where they read cleanly, while team colors and side designs carry across the open sections.
mesh-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: This is athletic mesh — an open knit whose entire purpose is airflow — with a bonded front panel for opacity and number legibility. It is the lightest and fastest-drying jersey fabric we offer, and our default recommendation for outdoor and un-air-conditioned play.
mesh-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Mesh has more give than a flat knit, so most players take their usual chest size rather than sizing up. If the jersey will be worn over a compression top, allow one size of room.
mesh-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Mesh jerseys are for heat — summer league, outdoor courts, tournament weekends, and gyms where the air conditioning is decorative. For the crispest possible match-day look, a flat-knit jersey holds a sharper line.
mesh-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Mesh trades a structured look for airflow. If your program wants the sharpest match-day appearance, choose from these.

lightweight-basketball-jerseys.sub: The Lightest Flat-Knit Jersey We Build
prose: A lightweight jersey is our standard sublimation polyester spun to a thinner gauge. It is not mesh — the face stays flat and solid, so artwork reproduces exactly as sharply as on a full-weight jersey — but there is meaningfully less fabric carrying heat and holding sweat.

This is the middle ground most programs actually want. Mesh is cooler but looks casual; full weight looks sharpest but runs hot. A lightweight flat knit keeps the clean match-day appearance and takes a real bite out of the heat, which in a Florida gym is usually the right compromise.

Thin fabric punishes bad construction, so the seams carry more of the load. Flatlock shoulder seams sit flush rather than standing proud, and the armhole and hem are bound so a lighter knit cannot stretch out of shape across a season.

benefits.rest: — the crisp look of a full-weight jersey with a real reduction in heat.
— unlike mesh, a flat knit reproduces fine type and thin outlines exactly.
— sit flush against the skin, which a light fabric cannot disguise.
— a thinner knit keeps its shape all season instead of stretching out.

lightweight-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: A thin, smooth face holds fine detail beautifully — small type, thin outlines and gradient work all reproduce cleanly where mesh would break them up. Note that a very light fabric shows a hint of the reverse face, so heavy solid blocks are worth reviewing at proof stage.
lightweight-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Built from a thinner gauge of our sublimation polyester. It keeps the flat face and sharp print of the full-weight jersey with noticeably less material, which is what puts it between a standard jersey and open mesh.
lightweight-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Lightweight jerseys are cut close to the standard fit. A player who prefers a roomier jersey should size up. Measure the chest at the fullest point with arms relaxed; polyester does not shrink, so order the size you want to wear.
lightweight-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: This is the right jersey for warm gyms where a program still wants a sharp match-day look. For the hottest outdoor play, mesh is cooler; for heavy contact, a full-weight jersey lasts longer.
lightweight-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: A lighter knit is not the toughest option for a contact-heavy program. If your kit takes a beating, these hold up longer.

sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.sub: The Classic Cut, and Still the Coolest
prose: The sleeveless jersey is the basketball silhouette — armholes cut open so the shoulder rotates freely through a full shooting motion with nothing to bind at the top of the stroke. It is what most leagues picture when they write a uniform rule, and what most players reach for by default.

The armhole is the whole design problem. Too shallow and it catches at the top of a shot; too deep and it gapes and shows the side. Ours is set at standard competitive depth with a bound edge that keeps its shape rather than curling out after a season of washes.

Leaving the shoulders and upper arms bare is also the most effective cooling any jersey cut can do, because that is where the body sheds heat fastest. In a Florida gym that is not a minor detail — it is the reason this cut has never gone away.

benefits.rest: — open enough for a full shooting motion without gaping at the side.
— hold their shape instead of curling after the first few washes.
— no sleeve seam breaking a design across the chest or back.
— the shoulders and upper arms are where the body sheds heat fastest, left bare.

sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: With no sleeve seams, the front and back are each a single unbroken canvas. Colors, logos, names, numbers and side panels are fully customizable, and a design can run right to the edge without a seam interrupting it.
sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: These are built from our sublimation polyester in a mid weight — light enough for a hot gym, structured enough that the armhole and hem hold their line through a full season.
sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Sleeveless jerseys are sized on chest measurement at the fullest point, arms relaxed. Check the armhole column if your league specifies a maximum depth. Between sizes, size down for a competitive fit or up for a relaxed one.
sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: The sleeveless cut suits most game situations and most Florida gyms. Where it does not work is a league or district that requires sleeves on a uniform.
sleeveless-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Some leagues and school districts require sleeves. If yours does, these are cut for the same play with sleeves attached.

short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.sub: For Leagues and Districts That Require Sleeves
prose: Plenty of Florida leagues, school districts and rec programs require a sleeved uniform, and a sleeveless jersey simply will not pass the check. This is the same competition jersey with a set-in short sleeve — built to satisfy that rule without giving up range.

The sleeve is where these go wrong elsewhere. Cut too tight and it grips the bicep at the top of a shot; cut too wide and it flaps. Ours is set with a raglan-influenced shoulder line and a relaxed bicep opening, so the arm moves through a full stroke without the sleeve pulling across the shoulder.

The sleeve also adds print area a sleeveless jersey does not have. Sponsor marks, memorial patches and season text move onto the sleeve, which frees the chest for the number and keeps the front from getting crowded.

benefits.rest: — the same competition jersey, built to satisfy a league or district uniform rule.
— the sleeve does not grip or pull across the shoulder at the top of a shot.
— sponsor marks and patches move to the sleeve, leaving the chest clear for the number.
— a raglan-influenced seam keeps a set-in sleeve from restricting the stroke.

short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Sleeves give you two extra print panels a sleeveless jersey does not have. Most programs use them for sponsor marks, patches or season text so the chest stays clean around the number. Everything prints full-color with no template limits.
short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: The same sublimation polyester as our sleeveless jerseys, in a mid weight. More of the arm is covered, so this cut runs a little warmer — if your venues are hot, ask about the lightweight or mesh version of the same sleeve pattern.
short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Sized on chest measurement, with the sleeve cut proportionally. A player with heavier arms should check the bicep column rather than relying on chest alone, and size up if it is close.
short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Short-sleeve jerseys are for programs whose league or district requires sleeves, and for cooler venues where a sleeve is welcome. If your rules permit sleeveless, that cut is cooler and cheaper.
short-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: If your league does not require sleeves, a sleeveless cut is cooler and gives more shoulder range for the same money.

long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.sub: Full-Arm Coverage for Cold Venues and Big Designs
prose: A long-sleeve basketball jersey covers the arm to the wrist. In Florida the reason is almost never the weather outside — it is the tournament venue held at 65 degrees, the early bus, and the two hours a roster spends sitting between games on a Saturday.

The sleeve has to be cut for basketball, not borrowed from another sport. Ours is narrow through the forearm so it does not bunch at the elbow, with a ribbed cuff that stays at the wrist instead of riding up on the first shooting motion. Players who wear a single compression sleeve often prefer this, in team colors, so the whole roster matches.

The sleeves also roughly double the printable area. A sponsor mark can run the length of the arm, a memorial patch gets real space, and the chest stays clear for the number — which is why programs with a lot to say on a jersey choose this cut.

benefits.rest: — stays flat through a shooting motion instead of bunching at the elbow.
— hold at the wrist rather than sliding to the elbow on the first shot.
— sleeves carry sponsors and patches so the chest stays clear for the number.
— which for a Florida program is an over-air-conditioned venue, not the outdoors.

long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Two full sleeves roughly double what you can print. Sponsor marks down the arm, memorial patches, championship years and season text all fit here without crowding the chest. Everything prints full-color, edge to edge, with no template limits.
long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Long-sleeve jerseys use a lighter knit than our short-sleeve version, deliberately — more of the body is covered, so the same weight would run hot. It is built to layer without adding bulk at the shoulder seam.
long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Sized on chest as usual, but check the sleeve-length column too. A player with long arms is usually better one size up even when the chest measurement says otherwise. Worn as a base layer under another jersey, take the normal size.
long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Long sleeves suit cold venues, winter tournaments, and programs with a lot to fit on a jersey. For a warm Florida gym with no air conditioning, this is the wrong cut.
long-sleeve-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Full sleeves are the wrong answer to a hot gym. If your venues run warm, these will be far more comfortable.

basketball-warm-up-jerseys.sub: What the Team Wears Before Anyone Checks a Roster
prose: A warm-up jersey is worn over the game jersey during warm-ups and on the bench, and it answers to no league rule at all. No mandated number size, no roster restriction, no color regulation — which makes it the freest garment in a uniform order and the one that carries the program's identity hardest.

The cut is built for pulling on over another jersey: roomier through the chest and shoulder, with a straight hem rather than a tapered one, so it comes off in one motion at the buzzer without catching on the game top underneath.

This is also the most photographed piece a program owns — warm-ups, team pictures, senior night, socials. A heat-pressed logo starts cracking around January; a sublimated one does not, which is why it is worth doing this piece properly rather than cheaply.

benefits.rest: — the front is free for a full-size logo, team name, or a season slogan.

benefits.strong: Cut to pull on over a game jersey
benefits.rest: — roomier through the chest and shoulder, with a straight hem that clears cleanly.
— dyed artwork does not crack the way a pressed logo does by mid-season.
— boosters and parents will wear a warm-up top; they will not wear a game jersey.

basketball-warm-up-jerseys.cardSub: Over-jersey layer · Full-color · Any logo size
basketball-warm-up-jerseys.customizationIntro: This is the freest layout in the whole order — no roster numbers to place and no league size rules to meet. Full-chest logos, a name across the back, sleeve marks, sponsor blocks and season text all work here in ways a game jersey cannot allow.
basketball-warm-up-jerseys.fabricIntro: Warm-up jerseys use a slightly heavier knit than a game jersey, because they are worn as an outer layer and need to hold their shape over another garment rather than sit against the skin.
basketball-warm-up-jerseys.sizingIntro: Size a warm-up one step up from the player's game jersey — it is meant to go on over the top. Measure the chest over the jersey that will actually be worn underneath, not over bare skin.
basketball-warm-up-jerseys.bestForIntro: Warm-up jerseys fit any program wanting a piece worn off the floor — warm-ups, bench, travel, photos and parent sales. They are not game garments and will not pass a uniform check.
basketball-warm-up-jerseys.notFitIntro: This is a layer, not a game jersey — no roster numbers, no league compliance. For the garment players compete in, start here.

youth-basketball-jerseys.sub: Game Jerseys Cut for Players Who Are Still Growing
prose: A youth game jersey has to solve something adult kit never does: the player wearing it in March is a different size than the one who was measured in October. A jersey that only fits half a season is a jersey bought twice.

The pattern allows for it without looking oversized on day one — extra length through the body and a slightly deeper armhole, so a season of growth is absorbed rather than outgrown. The neckline is bound to stay comfortable as shoulders broaden.

Numbers are printed a size larger than adult kit as standard. In a rec gym, officials and parents are reading from much further back than in a high school arena, and the extra size costs nothing at the print stage.

benefits.rest: — extra body length and a deeper armhole so the jersey still fits by February.
— readable from the back of a rec gym, at no extra cost.
— hot wash, tumble dry, no care ritual: the color is inside the fiber.
— a year-two replacement arrives the same shade as the rest of the set.

youth-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Youth jerseys print full-color with numbers set one size larger than adult kit by default. Team colors, logos, player names and sponsor marks are all available; most youth leagues keep the design simple so a whole league's worth of teams stays affordable.
youth-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: The same sublimation polyester as our adult jerseys in a slightly softer finish. Younger players notice fabric against the skin far more than adults do, and an uncomfortable jersey gets complained about for a whole season.
youth-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Youth sizing runs on height and chest together; where the two disagree, follow the chest. For a season-long order, size up — a jersey slightly large in November fits properly by February.
youth-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Youth jerseys fit leagues, middle school programs and rec teams buying game kit. For practice, youth practice jerseys cost far less and take the same abuse.
youth-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: This is game kit. For weeknight training and scrimmages, these cost a fraction and wear just as hard.

blank-basketball-jerseys.sub: Undecorated Jerseys, Ready for Your Own Decorator
prose: A blank jersey is the finished garment with no names, numbers or logos on it — the same cut, the same fabric, the same construction, decorated later by whoever you choose. It exists for programs that already have a local decorator, or that need stock on hand before a roster is settled.

The usual reason is timing. A team that does not know its roster in August cannot order numbered jerseys in August, but it can order blanks, hold them, and have them numbered the week the squad is final. Leagues buying for twelve teams do the same in reverse: one bulk blank order, decorated per team.

Blanks accept screen print, heat transfer, vinyl and embroidery, so your decorator is not limited by our process. A note worth having: because these are polyester, ask your decorator about dye migration — a low-temperature transfer avoids the pink haze cheap vinyl can pull out of a red jersey.

benefits.strong: Order before the roster is set
benefits.rest: — hold stock in August and number it the week the squad is final.
— screen print, vinyl, transfer or embroidery; your decorator is not tied to our process.
— identical cut, fabric and construction to our decorated jerseys.
— nothing to proof and no artwork stage, so blanks ship several days sooner.

blank-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Blanks are the one product here where the customization is the base garment itself — color, cut, fabric and trim. Names, numbers and logos are deliberately left off for your own decorator to add. If you would rather we handle decoration, any of our printed jerseys covers that.
blank-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Blanks are built from the same sublimation polyester as our decorated jerseys. Worth flagging to your decorator: polyester can dye-migrate under high heat, so a low-temperature transfer is the safe choice on strong base colors.
blank-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Sized exactly like our decorated jerseys — chest at the fullest point, arms relaxed. Because blanks are often ordered before a roster is final, most programs order a spread of sizes rather than a per-player list.
blank-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Blanks are right for programs with their own decorator, unsettled rosters, and leagues buying in bulk to decorate per team. If you want finished jerseys with names and numbers, order a decorated style instead.
blank-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: Blanks arrive with nothing on them. If you want jerseys ready to play in, choose a decorated style.

plain-basketball-jerseys.sub: One Clean Color, Numbers Only — Nothing Else
prose: A plain jersey is a single solid team color with numbers, and deliberately nothing else. No side panels, no gradient, no sponsor block. It is not the same thing as a blank: a blank has no decoration at all, while a plain jersey is finished and ready to play in.

Programs choose plain for two very different reasons. Some want the classic look — a solid jersey with clean numerals still reads as the most serious uniform in most gyms. Others want the cheapest finished jersey available, and a single-color layout is the least expensive thing to produce.

With no pattern to hide behind, the details carry the whole garment. The number font, its size, and the outline weight are the entire design, so those are the choices worth spending time on at proof stage rather than rushing.

benefits.rest: — a single-color layout is the least expensive thing to produce, and it shows in the price.
— unlike a blank, this arrives numbered and finished; nothing else is needed.
— a simple layout means a replacement jersey in year three matches the originals precisely.
— a solid jersey with clean numerals reads as the most serious uniform in most gyms.

plain-basketball-jerseys.cardSub: Solid color · Numbers only · Lowest cost
plain-basketball-jerseys.customizationIntro: Plain jerseys keep customization to base color, number style and an optional small team mark. That restraint is the point and the price. If you want side panels, gradients or full artwork, our sublimated and custom-printed jerseys carry all of it.
plain-basketball-jerseys.fabricIntro: Built from the same sublimation polyester as our full-design jerseys. A plain jersey is not a cheaper fabric — it is the same garment with a simpler layout, which is where the saving actually comes from.
plain-basketball-jerseys.sizingIntro: Sized on chest at the fullest point, arms relaxed, exactly as our other jerseys. Polyester does not shrink, so order the size you intend to wear.
plain-basketball-jerseys.bestForIntro: Plain jerseys fit tight budgets, large roster counts, and programs that want the classic solid look. If your identity depends on a logo or a distinctive pattern, a full-design jersey is worth the difference.
plain-basketball-jerseys.notFitIntro: A single solid color cannot carry a detailed identity. If your program has a logo or pattern that matters, choose one of these.

black-basketball-jersey.sub: The Away Kit Almost Every Program Owns
prose: Black is the most-ordered away color in basketball, and the reason is practical before it is aesthetic: it goes with every accent color a program might already own. A school whose primary is orange, teal, gold or maroon can put it on black and it works, which is not true of most other grounds.

It carries a real trade-off in Florida. A black jersey absorbs noticeably more radiant heat than a white one, which matters on an outdoor court in May and matters not at all in an air-conditioned gym in January. Programs that play outdoors often order black for away games and white for home for exactly this reason.

One production note worth knowing: sublimation prints from light to dark, so a black ground is produced by dyeing the whole panel rather than by leaving fabric bare. That makes color consistency across a large run more demanding, which is why we match and store your exact black once and reuse it for every reorder.

benefits.rest: — orange, teal, gold or maroon all read cleanly on black, which is why it is the default away kit.
— floor dust and scuffing show far less than on a light ground over a long season.
— a dyed black panel is demanding to reproduce, so the shade is stored and reused for every reorder.
— a light numeral on black is the highest-contrast combination in the sport.

black-basketball-jersey.customizationIntro: Black is a ground, not a limit — accent panels, numbers, names, logos and sponsor marks all print full-color over it. Light numerals give the strongest contrast; if your accent is a dark color, we will flag it at proof stage rather than let it disappear on the court.
black-basketball-jersey.fabricIntro: Built from sublimation polyester with the black dyed through the panel rather than left as base fabric. If your program plays outdoors in Florida heat, ask about the mesh version — an open weave takes most of the heat penalty out of a dark jersey.
black-basketball-jersey.sizingIntro: Measure the chest at the fullest point with arms relaxed. Dark jerseys read slightly slimmer than light ones at the same size, which is worth knowing if you are matching a black away kit to a white home kit for the same roster.
black-basketball-jersey.bestForIntro: Black suits away kits, indoor programs, and any team whose accent color needs a neutral ground. For hot outdoor play, a white or light jersey stays measurably cooler.
black-basketball-jersey.notFitIntro: A dark jersey absorbs more heat than a light one, which is real on an outdoor Florida court. For those venues, consider these.

white-basketball-shirt.sub: The Traditional Home Color, and the Coolest One
prose: White is the traditional home color in basketball, and in Florida it has a second advantage that has nothing to do with tradition: it reflects radiant heat rather than absorbing it. On an outdoor court in May the difference between a white shirt and a black one is genuinely measurable.

White is also the hardest ground to produce well, because there is nowhere to hide. Any inconsistency in the knit shows, and a thin white fabric becomes translucent under bright gym lighting. Ours is built to a heavier opacity standard specifically for that — a white shirt that goes see-through under lights is not a uniform.

The honest downside is upkeep. White shows court dust, sweat marks and grass in a way no other color does, so programs that choose it usually order a second shirt per player. It looks the sharpest of anything on this site, and it asks for the most care in return.

benefits.strong: Reflects heat instead of absorbing it
benefits.rest: — the coolest ground you can put a player in on an outdoor Florida court.
— heavier than our standard knit so it does not go translucent under bright gym lighting.

benefits.strong: Every accent color works on it
benefits.rest: — white is the most flexible ground for a program with an unusual primary color.

benefits.strong: Photographs best of anything we make
benefits.rest: — which is why it is still the traditional choice for home and for team pictures.

white-basketball-shirt.customizationIntro: White gives full-color artwork the cleanest possible ground — every accent reproduces at its true value rather than shifting against a dyed panel. Dark numerals give the strongest contrast; a very light accent on white will be flagged at proof rather than printed to disappear.
white-basketball-shirt.fabricIntro: This uses a heavier-opacity knit than our colored shirts. That is deliberate: white is the only ground where a thin fabric becomes see-through under arena lighting, so it is built with more body specifically to avoid it.
white-basketball-shirt.sizingIntro: Measure the chest at the fullest point with arms relaxed. White reads slightly fuller than a dark shirt at the same size — worth allowing for if you are matching a white home kit against a black away kit on the same roster.
white-basketball-shirt.bestForIntro: White is right for home kits, outdoor play, and team photos. It is the highest-maintenance color we sell, so most programs choosing it order two per player rather than one.
white-basketball-shirt.notFitIntro: White shows everything a court can put on it. If your season is heavy on outdoor or practice wear, a darker ground stays presentable longer.

blue-basketball-jersey.sub: The Most-Ordered School Color, Matched Exactly
prose: Blue is the most common primary color in American school athletics, which makes it the color where getting the exact shade right matters most. "Blue" covers navy, royal, columbia, carolina and a dozen institutional variants, and a program whose banners are navy does not want a royal jersey.

That is a color-management problem, not a design one. We match to your specified value — a Pantone reference, a school style guide, or a physical sample — and store it against your account, so the jerseys you reorder in year three are the same blue as the ones you bought in year one.

Blue is also the most forgiving ground to design on. White, gold, silver and orange all read strongly against it, so number contrast is rarely a problem, and a navy jersey hides court marks nearly as well as a black one while running measurably cooler in the sun.

benefits.strong: Your exact blue, not our idea of it
benefits.rest: — matched to a Pantone value, style guide or physical sample before anything is printed.
— a year-three reorder is the same navy as the year-one order, which is the usual complaint with blue.

benefits.strong: Strongest accent range of any ground
benefits.rest: — white, gold, silver and orange all read clearly against blue.

benefits.strong: Hides court marks, runs cooler than black
benefits.rest: — navy gets most of black's practical advantage with less heat absorption.

blue-basketball-jersey.cardSub: Exact shade matched · Any accent · Full-color
blue-basketball-jersey.customizationIntro: The most important customization here is the blue itself. Send a Pantone number, a school style guide, or a jersey you already own, and we match to it. Everything else — accents, numbers, names, logos, sponsor marks — prints full-color over that matched ground.
blue-basketball-jersey.fabricIntro: Standard sublimation polyester with the blue dyed through the panel. Navy absorbs somewhat more heat than a light ground but noticeably less than black, which is part of why it is the most-used school color in warm states.
blue-basketball-jersey.sizingIntro: Measure the chest at the fullest point, arms relaxed. Mid- and dark-blue jerseys read slightly slimmer than white at the same size, so if your program runs a navy away and a white home kit, expect them to look a little different on the same player.
blue-basketball-jersey.bestForIntro: Blue suits school programs, long-running teams, and anyone who has to match an existing institutional color. It works equally as a home or away kit.
blue-basketball-jersey.notFitIntro: If you do not need a specific institutional shade, a simpler plain jersey gets you the same garment for less.

red-basketball-uniform.sub: The Most Saturated Color on Court, Jersey and Shorts Together
prose: Red is the most visually saturated color in a basketball gym, which is why so many programs build an identity on it. It is also, technically, the most demanding color to reproduce consistently — small variations in dye load show up as a shift between orange-red and blue-red that the eye catches instantly across a roster of twelve.

That is a production discipline problem. Every piece in a red order is printed in the same run from the same color file, which is how a set stays uniform; ordering jerseys now and shorts in three months is precisely how programs end up with a set that does not quite match.

One warning worth passing to anyone decorating red kit locally: red polyester is the classic dye-migration case. A high-temperature vinyl press can pull dye out of the fabric and turn white lettering pink over a few weeks. If you add anything after delivery, use a low-temperature transfer.

benefits.strong: Jersey and shorts in one run
benefits.rest: — the only reliable way to keep a red set matching, since red shows the smallest dye shift.
— so a replacement piece next season does not arrive a half-shade orange.

benefits.strong: Highest visual presence in a gym
benefits.rest: — no color reads stronger from the bleachers, which is why identities get built on it.
— sublimated numbers are in the fiber; nothing is pressed on top to bleed later.
